Second, uncritically, through apologetic affirmation. The second is the surest method of destruction.
Columbus came to America without papers and without an entry visa from the Aztecs or the Indians.
Discoveries take place without the visa of the people being discovered. That is actually part of what discovery means.
E.[rnst] J.[ünger] had neither feeling nor understanding for my situation as an outlaw. He did not even see it.
The appalling thrift of this completely self-enclosed monad who makes use of every last idea that occurs to him.
Not a window and not a door opening onto another human being.
“I would rather not see the poor throat that produces it,” Peterheinrich [Kirchhoff] said.
The poorest, narrowest voice I have ever heard in my life.
A man defending himself is more vicious than a man attacking.

When he is defending himself, he feels that he is in the right. That makes him cruel and gives him the clear conscience he needs to punish the defeated enemy—or even to “educate” him, meaning to inject a different soul into him.
How rich we were in ideas! How full of sudden insights! How extravagantly we wasted ourselves in conversation!

I rejoice in that waste when I look at these people today who make use of absolutely everything: these miserly petty capitalists, these penny-pinchers with their ideas, these men who ration out their witty remarks.
I am the only one capable of judging this polished economy of spirit.
[later deleted:] And Paul Adams is the only person I could tell this to.
The medieval ghetto was not based on a fear of germs. The existentialist existence of Mr. Jaspers, by contrast, rests on germ-phobia.
As a member of bourgeois society, I am dead.
Now the Parsi dance begins over my grave.
But that is still quite harmless. There are no graves anymore. We are cremated, and our ashes are scattered into the air. The ashes refuse to disappear. They drift as dust through every land.
Anyone who lays down broad general clauses and works with deliberately vague concepts must keep a very firm grip on things.
Otherwise the vagueness turns back on him with terrible force.

Ernst Jünger has become a prima donna, a complete monad, with Léon Bloy hanging on his façade like a blind window. So when a block this heavily armored in its own ego shows even the faintest glimmer of interest that is not purely solipsistic—in this case, an interest in Bernanos—I am moved, and I lend him a book about Bernanos that does not even belong to me. I knock, and—listen!—a bell rings, and a door opens into other worlds. And so the door is opened to me.
Today E.[rnst] J.[ünger] seems to me like his own father—the father he became to himself in Paris in Strahlungen. He is wreckage washed ashore from the Wilhelmine age. So is Thomas Mann.
What people take for restoration is merely wreckage that has been rescued from the shore. Nothing more.
“God bless our shore,” pray yesterday’s persecuted and today’s persecutors.
To handle vague concepts, to keep things suspended, to evade alternatives imposed from outside—only someone who is openly very strong, or secretly very strong, can do that.
Germany wants to keep its own position between East and West deliberately undefined.
A word like Großraum—“large space”—is too clear.
In an age of deliberate, systematic blurring, when every concept is consciously mixed up with every other, it is foolish to use precisely defined words.
The same applies to the definition of the political, whose core is the distinction between friend and enemy.
All powers agree on one thing: they persecute the discoverer of such words and concepts.
The secret behind the hostility toward the discoverer.
The people who are to be discovered demand that I first obtain an entry visa from them.
Columbus did not have a visa from the Aztecs or the Incas either. So they simply beat me to death.
The fate of Miorița: the good lamb and the good shepherd.
Man is the shepherd of Being.
People cannot tolerate being recognized, much less discovered.
No one likes to be completely understood. That is why a person sees the man who has understood him as an enemy.
Everyone—even the righteous black-marketeer—is convinced that the better you know him and the more completely you understand him, the more you must love and admire him.

What follows from all these undeniable truths and obvious realities? It follows that Don Capisco—Don “I Understand”—has every chance of being declared hostis generis humani, an enemy of the human race.
I live in a dreadful exile, exul in patria mea—an exile in my own country.
The Germans are a people of metaphysicians and technicians, but neither jurists nor moralists.
Reading a few extracts from a book by Amédée Ponceau (Timoléon: Reflections on Tyranny) moves me to tears.
A voice like Ponceau’s would be impossible in Germany. It is an almost miraculous consolation to hear such a voice coming from France.

Ernst Jünger is like many famous figures who stand on the public stage of literature or art. They concentrate all their strength on their public appearance. They call that concentrating on “their work.” They gather themselves for the moments of their public vocation, even when those moments are spent sitting alone at a desk. They do not waste themselves in private life, in conversation, or in any exchange that cannot be turned directly into something useful. They practice a well-founded economy with their strength and their radiance. They let nothing go to waste. They make use of everything that can possibly be made useful, without giving any of themselves away.
As a result, their entire presence lies in their public work.
Their whole existence is absorbed into publicity.
You should see them on stage or read their books.
There is little point in dealing with them outside that setting.
You are “handled” by them. You are identified, sorted, and put to use according to their methods for extracting value from whatever can somehow be used.
As a little sweet, you are handed a sentence they printed years ago. They are absent whenever they are not appearing before their audience or working for that audience.
Truly: genuine workers in the publicity machine.
What remains is not even silence. It is zero.
When absolutely everything that can possibly be used is put to use, there is no remainder at all.

Someone puts on the fog-cap of a half-mythological disguise. He retreats into suggestive landscapes and spaces. He paints Böcklin-like landscapes in historical and political colors. He no longer speaks of Jews, but of Parsis, although everyone can see that he is talking about himself and the Jews, and so on. He no longer speaks of Nazis, but of the Demos and the governor.
No longer of the SS, but of Mauritanians.
No longer of himself, but of Commander Lucius.
In this way he can speak about himself and his age, use every attraction of a roman à clef, and still, in the end, say nothing definite enough to pin down.
The eager reader, who now wants to know what the author actually thinks about the Jews or the Nazis, is left just as fooled as the author remains free of commitment.
A very practical method of protection through coded language, and highly recommended in times when the fronts change quickly.
One speaks very wisely and at great length, yet never commits oneself.

One says enough to fill a thick book and still ends up saying nothing dangerous, only painting pseudo-mythological scenery. But this is probably the correct method for publishing on current affairs in a state where everything requires a license.
Non possum directe scribere de eo qui potest directe proscribere.
I cannot write directly about the man who can directly proscribe me.

The present international debate about Vitoria and the legality of the Spanish Conquest is the sad background music accompanying the destruction of the glorious European overseas empires and the transformation of India and Indonesia into sovereign states and equal members of the United Nations.

At Yalta and Potsdam, the Anglo-Saxons pursued a Third Force policy: unconsciousness pushed all the way into lethargy, the congenital condition of every Third Force, the mentality of the No-No Zone.

“Having studied philosophy and theology, the history of the Church and of nations, and papal documents for more than twenty years, and having read and reread Bernanos, Péguy, and Drumont, I believe I know what I am talking about.”
In 635, the most distinguished Christian in Damascus handed the keys of Damascus to the Muslims.
“For my part, I prefer Charles Martel.”
The Catholics are the anarchists and nihilists of the communist order.
He thinks the Russians will abandon the schism the moment they spit out communism.
The entire conceptual armory for this struggle has been lying ready for more than twenty years. He does not know it.
